cim: SEC Faces Questions Over Artificial Intelligence in Capital Markets
cim_eredeti: SEC Faces Questions Over Artificial Intelligence in Capital Markets
szoveg_eredeti:
The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has not issued regulations specifically targeting artificial intelligence use in capital markets, even as financial firms deploy the technology across trading, compliance and client services, according to a new Congressional Research Service (CRS) report. ​

The report identifies unresolved policy concerns, including accountability gaps when AI systems fail, risks from market concentration among a small number of AI developers, and potentially misleading "AI washing" disclosures, framing them as issues for congressional oversight and possible legislation.

The National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020 (P.L. 116-283, Division E) defines artificial intelligence as "a machine-based system that can make predictions, recommendations, or decisions influencing real or virtual environments." Common capital markets applications include investment management, algorithmic trading, robo-advising, anti-money laundering compliance and back-office productivity support.

In April 2025, the Trump administration's Office of Management and Budget issued Memorandum M-25-21, directing agencies, including the SEC, to develop AI strategies and build an AI-ready federal workforce. The SEC issued its compliance plan in September 2025 and launched an AI task force in August 2025, reporting 60 internal AI use cases that year. The SEC withdrew a 2023 proposed rule addressing conflicts of interest associated with predictive data analytics in June 2025, along with other rules proposed under the previous administration.

As of October, the SEC had received petitions for rulemaking seeking mandatory AI governance and risk management disclosures in public filings but had not indicated whether it would pursue AI-specific rulemaking. The SEC's fiscal 2027 examination priorities continue to emphasize AI disclosures, AI-related risks and cybersecurity under existing securities laws.

The Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act, H.R. 4801, sponsored by Rep. J. French Hill (R-AR), would establish AI innovation labs at the SEC and other financial regulators, allowing test projects to operate with relief from certain regulations. The bill was placed on the Union Calendar on June 24. The AI Act of 2024, H.R. 10262, sponsored by Rep. Maxine Waters (D-CA), would have required the SEC to study AI's benefits and risks for capital markets. The House Financial Services Committee referred it in November 2024, but it did not advance before the 118th Congress adjourned.

The SEC has not adopted AI-specific capital markets regulations or announced whether it intends to pursue such rules. Petitions seeking mandatory AI governance and risk management disclosures remain part of the regulatory debate, while the agency continues examining AI-related risks under existing securities frameworks.

H.R. 4801 has been placed on the Union Calendar and is eligible for consideration by the full House, but no floor vote has been scheduled.
